messages.author: e413f15f534b3710
messages.subject: memory issue with multithreading
parts:
Dear all,

I'm working on implementing a fairly general mixed-effects model class in TMB, with many interesting special cases. In general, the model works as expected, but as I recently ran a validation exercise that involved recreating a TMB model object several times within a loop I noticed some strange memory leak/release issue: It seems that when I use multiple cores for the calculations (by setting openmp()), the memory is gradually filled up (in the most extreme cases up to the point when the process is killed) and I can't release the memory (by deleting the object and even manually calling the garbage collector) unless I restart the whole R session. Everything works fine when I set openmp(1).

I created a simple example that hopefully highlights the problem. The input data structure is a bit complicated at the moment, but I generated an example from data("rats", package = "survival") and dumped it into the file input_dat.R. When I run ex.R with more than one cores and look at htop in Ubuntu, the memory usage increases very quickly with a couple of GBs.

Am I doing something wrong? Do you have any suggestions how I could solve this problem? Any comments on the code itself are also appreciated.

parts:
Hi Kasper,

Thanks for your reply. Yesterday I checked it on a colleague's
computer (similar configuration) and I could reproduce the problem. As
you suggested, I also tried a simpler example without extra package
dependencies, and I get the same issue with the linreg_parallel
example even without doing the optimization step:

library(TMB)
compile("linreg_parallel.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("linreg_parallel"))

set.seed(123)
x <- seq(0, 10, length=50001)
data <- list(Y=rnorm(length(x)) + x, x=x)
parameters <- list(a=0, b=0, logSigma=0)

for (i in 1:1000) {
obj <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL="linreg_parallel", silent = TRUE)
}

If I run this long enough, I can fill up the memory until the process
gets killed.

Do you have any suggestions how I could make the example more
convincing and reproducible? The fact that you didn't experience the
problem suggests that it is dependent on the system configuration or a
software component.


Thanks,

Balint

Hi there. I also have the same problem.

If my .cpp is in parallel, and I try to optimized it, sometimes I receive an error like that: Error : C stack usage 1047298757980 is too close to the limit (The actual number differs every time I run)

I followed this link to address the Error : C stack usage issue, which helped me only a little bit on my machine. However, to solve it once for all, I also need to decrease the number of threads, or discard the parallel processing.

"Example:" I was running my code in a 92Gb RAM server with 24 threads for a multivariate COM-Poisson model. Even whit this set up, I am only able to use 4 out of 24 threads to complete the task, without the Error: C stack usage 

I can also try to provide a reproducible example for this, in case you think that it is useful.

Best regards

parts:
Guilherme, The problem you experience is different - very likely same as this: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/310
Note you can use the search functionality in gihub issues...

There are currently many known issues with parallization affecting stability (thread safety and memory issues). In general, the performance gain is highly problem specific and may even be negative (a slowdown), so you better think twice before using TMB-parallelization in your own R packages.
You need to at least be aware of the following:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/316
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/310
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/303
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/189

On top of that there are potential installation difficulties (platform specific issues).

On Friday, 17 July 2020 at 07:28:41 UTC-3 kasper.k...@gmail.com wrote:
Guilherme, The problem you experience is different - very likely same as this: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/310
Note you can use the search functionality in gihub issues...

There are currently many known issues with parallization affecting stability (thread safety and memory issues). In general, the performance gain is highly problem specific and may even be negative (a slowdown), so you better think twice before using TMB-parallelization in your own R packages.
You need to at least be aware of the following:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/316
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/310
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/303
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/189

On top of that there are potential installation difficulties (platform specific issues).


On Wednesday, July 15, 2020 at 3:21:02 PM UTC+2, Guilherme Parreira wrote:
Hi there. I also have the same problem.

If my .cpp is in parallel, and I try to optimized it, sometimes I receive an error like that: Error : C stack usage 1047298757980 is too close to the limit (The actual number differs every time I run)

I followed this link to address the Error : C stack usage issue, which helped me only a little bit on my machine. However, to solve it once for all, I also need to decrease the number of threads, or discard the parallel processing.

"Example:" I was running my code in a 92Gb RAM server with 24 threads for a multivariate COM-Poisson model. Even whit this set up, I am only able to use 4 out of 24 threads to complete the task, without the Error: C stack usage 

I can also try to provide a reproducible example for this, in case you think that it is useful.

Best regards
